# ChatGPT web search for OpenCode V2

[![Checks](https://github.com/DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch/actions/workflows/test.yml)

Search the web in OpenCode using your existing **ChatGPT subscription**—no
additional API key or search service. Registers ChatGPT in V2's native search
provider picker and uses the built-in `websearch` tool, not a replacement tool
or an MCP server.

No runtime dependencies. Written in strict TypeScript and tested against
**OpenCode 2.0.28**. **V1 is not supported.**

## Install

Add the GitHub package to your global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or a
project's `opencode.jsonc`), preserving your other settings:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["github:DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch#v1.1.2"],
  "websearch": { "provider": "chatgpt" },
}
```

OpenCode installs GitHub packages automatically. Alternatively, install globally
using the CLI, then choose **ChatGPT** in the normal search provider picker:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch#v1.1.2'
```

Connect and select a ChatGPT subscription using **`/connect` → OpenAI** if you
haven't already. Ask OpenCode to search, for example:

```text
Search official Zephyr documentation for the next RTOS LTS release and its planned date.
```

The package is distributed through GitHub; it is not currently published to npm.
The `v1.1.2` tag pins a release; use `#main` only if you want development updates.
If a newly installed plugin hasn't appeared, run `opencode service restart`.

## Configuration

Search defaults to **`gpt-6-luna`** (GPT-6 Luna), independently of the conversation model.
V2's search provider interface receives a query and cancellation signal, not the
session's selected model. You can choose another backend model your subscription
supports:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch#v1.1.2",
      "options": {
        "model": "gpt-6-luna",
        "timeout": 120000,
      },
    },
  ],
  "websearch": { "provider": "chatgpt" },
}
```

| Option    | Default      | Description                                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `model`   | `gpt-6-luna` | Backend model ID, without a provider prefix.                                                           |
| `timeout` | `120000`     | HTTP request/stream timeout in milliseconds (1–300000).                                                |
| `default` | `false`      | Select ChatGPT unless search is explicitly disabled. Prefer `websearch.provider` for normal selection. |

Omit `websearch.provider` to use the native picker instead. The plugin does not
override your selection or saved consent unless explicitly configured to do so.
OpenCode's usual search permissions still apply. Set `websearch: false` to disable
search, or remove the plugin entry to uninstall it.

## How it works

- Registers through `ctx.websearch.transform` with provider ID `chatgpt` and
  plugin ID `opencode.chatgpt-websearch`.
- Resolves the active OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth credential on every query. OpenCode
  manages token refresh and account switching; the plugin never reads token files
  or the database and never stores credentials itself.
- Sends the query to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` with the
  native `web_search` tool enabled. The endpoint is fixed and redirects are
  rejected to protect subscription tokens.
- Returns a clearly labeled synthesized summary linked to ChatGPT, followed by
  deduplicated source URLs and titles. The ChatGPT link is **not an evidence
  source**; cite the actual source links.
- Handles streamed UTF-8/SSE, citations, cancellation, bounded response size,
  timeouts, and terminal failures. Rejects answers without a web-search invocation
  or successful completion rather than presenting model knowledge as search.

## Limitations and troubleshooting

This is an **unofficial integration**, unaffiliated with OpenAI or OpenCode. It
uses the same ChatGPT/Codex backend as the upstream provider; backend changes or
account restrictions may break it. Search uses your subscription allowance and
depends on your account's model and web-search access.

- **Authentication error:** select a ChatGPT OAuth login under OpenAI, not an API
  key. Reconnect through `/connect` if needed. Only V2's `chatgpt-browser` and
  `chatgpt-headless` methods are supported.
- **Model/tool unavailable:** set `options.model` to a model supported by your
  subscription and the Codex backend. Access varies by account.
- **HTTP 429:** wait for your subscription rate limit to reset; this plugin does
  not implement its own retry or automatic provider fallback.
- **Plugin not listed:** check `opencode plugin list` and the service logs; verify
  you're running V2. Restart the service if configuration watching didn't pick up
  the installation.

Do not paste OAuth tokens, authorization headers, or unredacted logs into issues.
See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Local development

```sh
git clone https://github.com/DavidNepozitek/opencode-chatgpt-websearch.git
cd opencode-chatgpt-websearch
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm check
```

Development requires Node.js 22.18+ and pnpm 11.27.0. Tests run offline with
synthetic credentials. SDK types, TypeScript, oxlint, and oxfmt are development-only
dependencies; installation by OpenCode requires no build or lifecycle scripts.
To test in OpenCode, configure the repository's absolute path in `plugins`.
V2 also discovers package directories under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` and
`.opencode/plugins/` automatically.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the source/test layout, commands, and
dependency-review policy. CI uses frozen lockfiles, SHA-pinned actions, minimal
permissions, dependency auditing, and CodeQL security analysis.

# Contributing

Use Node.js 22.18+ and **pnpm 11.27.0** (pinned in `package.json`). Run:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm check
pnpm audit:dependencies
```

`pnpm check` runs strict TypeScript checking, oxlint, oxfmt's format check, offline
tests, and a declaration/JavaScript build. Use `pnpm format` to format changes.
Tests use synthetic credentials and never require a real ChatGPT login.

## Layout

- `server.ts`: thin compatibility entrypoint for OpenCode's local-directory discovery.
- `src/index.ts`: OpenCode V2 plugin registration and credential resolution.
- `src/options.ts`: runtime validation of plugin options.
- `src/chatgpt/client.ts`: authenticated request and sanitized transport errors.
- `src/chatgpt/sse.ts`: bounded UTF-8/SSE framing and cancellation.
- `src/chatgpt/stream.ts`: runtime validation and search-result assembly.
- `tests/`: client, stream, and host-integration tests with shared synthetic fixtures.
- `.github/`: SHA-pinned CI, CodeQL, and Dependabot configuration.

The installed package exports TypeScript directly, which OpenCode loads natively.
SDK imports are **type-only**; there are no production dependencies or installation
lifecycle scripts. `pnpm compile` emits an optional `dist/` directory for development,
but package installation does not need to build anything.

Do not add a root `build`, `prepare`, or installation lifecycle script: npm's Git
fetcher uses these names as triggers for dependency preparation, which breaks
direct GitHub installation in OpenCode. The regression tests enforce this.

Treat every parsed backend value as `unknown` until validated. Keep the endpoint
fixed, reject redirects, bound untrusted input, and do not attach raw errors as
`cause` when they can contain secrets. Add regression tests for security changes.

Keep dependencies exact and commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Installation scripts are
disabled and fresh dependencies have a one-day release-age floor. Provenance
downgrade checks have no exceptions. Node types track the current release, while
CI retains Node 22, 24, and 26 to verify the supported runtime baseline.

Open pull requests against `main`; CI and CodeQL must pass. Main requires a review;
repository administrators can bypass review **through a pull request only** for
solo maintenance, not by directly pushing to main. Release tags cannot be updated
or deleted. Do not auto-merge
dependency updates without review. Report security issues privately as described
in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# Security

Never include ChatGPT OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, account identifiers,
authorization headers, or private queries in public issues or pull requests.
The tests use synthetic credentials; no real credential is needed to contribute.

## Runtime protections

The plugin resolves credentials through OpenCode's integration API and sends
access tokens only to the fixed ChatGPT Codex endpoint. It does not store tokens,
read authentication files, or follow HTTP redirects. Request errors intentionally
omit backend response bodies and raw transport errors. Header values and queries
are validated before network calls. Incoming JSON is validated at runtime;
response/event sizes, completion state, UTF-8 decoding, and cancellation are
checked before results are returned.

## Supply-chain and repository protections

The package has no runtime dependencies and no install/build lifecycle scripts.
Development dependencies and pnpm are pinned; the lockfile includes registry
integrities. pnpm disables lifecycle scripts, rejects exotic transitive sources,
enforces a one-day release-age floor, and checks provenance downgrades without
exceptions.

CI uses SHA-pinned actions, read-only tokens by default, no persisted checkout
credentials, frozen installs, oxlint, strict TypeScript, offline tests, and a
dependency audit. Only the CodeQL job receives `security-events: write`.
Dependabot proposes reviewed updates; it does not auto-merge them.

GitHub secret scanning/push protection and private vulnerability reporting are
enabled. Main-branch protections require checks and restrict history rewriting;
maintainers review changes through pull requests. No controls guarantee the
absence of vulnerabilities, and OpenAI backend behavior is outside this project's
control.

Search queries are sent to ChatGPT and may contain private information. Review
OpenCode's `websearch` permission rules and avoid searching for secrets. Retrieved
content and model summaries are untrusted; verify consequential claims against
the linked sources.

Report vulnerabilities privately through the repository's **Security → Report a
vulnerability** interface. Please do not disclose credentials or exploitable
security details in public issues.
